 Seremban High Court orders six former Undangs and chieftains to face second contempt proceedings
 TheEdge 
 Tue, Nov 17, 2026 02:03pm - 18 hours 
 View Original 
 KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 17) : The High Court in Seremban on Tuesday granted leave for the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, to initiate a second contempt proceeding against six former Undangs and chieftains involved in the ongoing Negeri Sembilan royal dispute.
 The second proceeding concerns the alleged evasion of service of court documents relating to the first contempt proceeding.
 Judge Roz Mawar Rozain made the decision following proceedings that concluded on Tuesday morning.
 The first contempt proceeding against the six arose from their participation in the installation and proclamation of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan on June 5, purportedly replacing the incumbent ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
 This followed the DKU and Raja Norazli obtaining a temporary injunction on the same day, barring DKU events pending the disposal of an originating summons filed by the six.
 The six are former Undangs Datuk Maarof Mat Rashid (Jelebu) and Datuk Abd Rahim Yasin (Rembau), Datuk Mubarak Thahak, whose status as the Undang of Sungai Ujong is disputed, and Datuk Muhammed Abdullah (Johol), as well as Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al Qadri and Datuk Shahbandar Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.
 Roz Mawar fixed Dec 15 for both contempt proceedings to be heard.
 "All of them must come for the proceedings on Dec 15," the judge said.
 The DKU and Raja Norazli were represented by Steven Thiru, David Mathew, Shafrin Halim, Gregory Das and Gurjeevan Singh Sachdev, while Zainuddin Omar represented the Tunku Besar of Tampin. Asmawi Ismail and Deidra Nur Azmi appeared for the remaining five.
 Thiru confirmed the outcome to The Edge when contacted after Tuesday's proceedings.
 The latest development follows the Court of Appeal's dismissal on Nov 4 of an application by the six Undangs and chieftains to stay the contempt proceedings pending an appeal against the committal order granted by Roz Mawar on July 8.
 A three-member appellate bench comprising Datuk Amarjeet Singh Serjit Singh, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab held that the issue of the six individuals' purported immunity should be determined during the substantive hearing of the committal proceedings, rather than beforehand.
 "The very issue ought to be fully ventilated and determined at the committal proceedings during the substantive stage," Amarjeet said when delivering the bench's decision.
 He also said the six had not come to court with clean hands in seeking the stay.
 The six had filed an originating summons in May seeking the production of the DKU minutes from a meeting that month which led to Mubarak's expulsion, a decision they disputed.
 In their preliminary objection to the originating summons, the DKU and Raja Norazli argued that matters concerning the DKU were non-justiciable. The originating summons remains pending.
